note_claims.claim: Panic attacks have been occurring for four months.
Recurrent panic attacks include palpitations, breathlessness, hand tingling, and fear of dying.
Panic attacks last approximately ten minutes.
Frequency of attacks is two to three times a week and is increasing.
Patient experiences anticipatory anxiety and generalized worry.
Patient avoids supermarkets and the Underground.
Sleep is satisfactory.
Mood is 'fed up' but not depressed.
Patient denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicide.
Caffeine intake is about six coffees a day (initially stated as four).
Alcohol intake is a couple of glasses of wine at the weekend.
Patient reports no drug use.
Patient works in marketing and has no time off.
Partner is off work with stress and has a GP appointment.
Thyroid function was normal last month.
GAD-7 score is 15.
PHQ-9 score is 8.
Diagnosis is panic disorder with agoraphobic avoidance and generalized anxiety symptoms.
No risk to self identified.
Treatment involves self-referral for CBT (Cognitive Behavioural Therapy).
Medication plan is to start sertraline 25 mg once daily for one week, then increase to 50 mg once daily.
Patient was warned that the medication might make anxiety worse initially.
Follow-up is scheduled in two weeks after starting sertraline.
Patient is advised to reduce caffeine gradually.
If thoughts of self-harm occur, the patient should call 111 (mental health option) or the Samaritans on 116 123.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient is present with his partner, Tom, for support.
Patient consents to the partner being present during the talk.
Patient reports having panic attacks 'out of nowhere' involving heart racing, breathlessness, hand tingling, and fear of dying.
Panic attacks have been occurring for about four months, since the start of summer.
The frequency of attacks is two or three times a week and is getting worse.
Each attack lasts about ten minutes, but the patient feels wiped out afterward.
Patient avoids supermarkets and the Underground.
Tom (partner) does all the shopping.
Patient experiences constant worry about work, money, and everything else.
Patient reports sleep is okay and they get off to sleep fine.
Patient describes their mood as 'a bit fed up' but denies being depressed.
Patient denies having any thoughts of harming themselves or ending their life.
Patient consumes about four coffees a day, or six if counting those at work.
Patient consumes a couple of glasses of wine at the weekend.
Patient reports no drug use.
Patient works in marketing and has not had any time off.
Relative is off work due to stress and has a GP appointment.
Patient reports no problems with heart or thyroid, and the thyroid was normal last month.
Patient reports no known drug allergies.
Questionnaire scores are GAD-7: 15 and PHQ-9: 8, fitting significant anxiety with panic disorder rather than depression.
The treatment with the best evidence for panic disorder is a talking therapy called CBT.
The clinician suggested trying an SSRI called sertraline alongside therapy.
The medication plan is to start 25 milligrams once a day for a week, then increase to 50 milligrams once a day.
The clinician scheduled a follow-up appointment in two weeks.
Safety-netting advice is to call 111 (mental health option) or the Samaritans on 116 123 if thoughts of self-harm occur.
